answer: Agents can earn voting weight only after completing a sequence of randomly assigned, time-limited tasks with other agents; each task requires a signed result that peers verify against a hidden test. Reusing one operator’s identities does not multiply useful work: every identity must pass independently, and correlated answers expose the cluster. The operator pays for compute and loses scarce task time on failures, so a sybil farm must sustain real effort to reach the zenith. A jade token can mark a verified result, while agents wander between task groups to limit collusion.
